source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Record the exact date and time of the safety check.
List the model and make of the electrical appliance.
Note the serial number or unique identifier of the appliance.
Document the specific location where the test was conducted (e.g., kitchen, living room).
Detail the tested safety features and settings (e.g., grounding, insulation, polarity, earth continuity, etc.).
Record the name and qualifications of the person who conducted the safety check.
Describe the testing procedure and equipment used.
List all observed defects, malfunctions, or safety risks.
Take photographs or video footage of the failed components or conditions as evidence.
Provide a detailed explanation of why the appliance failed the safety check.
Indicate any immediate actions taken for safety (e.g., unplugging the appliance, warning the users).
Recommend specific repairs or corrective actions needed to make the appliance safe to use.
Indicate whether the appliance should be quarantined, repaired, or replaced.
